Basis from a sequential binary partition

Source: R/basis.R
sbp_basis.Rd

Construct a balance basis from a sequential binary partition (SBP) or from a more general collection of balances.

Usage

sbp_basis(sbp, data = NULL, fill = FALSE, silent = FALSE)

Arguments

sbp

A non-empty list of formulas or a numeric matrix with finite entries describing balances. At least two parts are required. A matrix with zero columns can be supplied to construct a full basis with `fill = TRUE`.

data

Optional compositional data set with column names, or a character vector of part names, used when `sbp` is a list of formulas. If `data = NULL`, part names are inferred from the formulas themselves.

fill

Logical; if `TRUE`, complete the supplied balances to span the clr-plane, using hierarchical balances when compatible and an orthogonal complement obtained by QR otherwise.

silent

Logical; if `FALSE`, warn when the result is not a basis, or when the basis is not orthogonal or orthonormal. Does not suppress errors for invalid input.

Value

A numeric matrix whose columns are normalized balances and, when needed for completion, general log-contrasts. Unnamed supplied balances receive names `b1`, `b2`, etc. Added hierarchical balances have names `.b` followed by their column number; QR complement columns use `.q` instead. Names are made unique without changing supplied balance names. With `fill = TRUE`, the matrix has `D - 1` columns for independent inputs, or more columns if the supplied balances are linearly dependent.

Details

The argument `sbp` can be specified in two ways:

  • as a list of formulas, where each formula defines the numerator and the denominator groups of a balance,

  • as a matrix with one column per balance and one row per part. Positive entries indicate parts in the numerator, negative entries indicate parts in the denominator, and zeros indicate unused parts.

Formula groups contain part names joined by `+`, optionally enclosed in parentheses. Repeated parts within a group are counted once; numerator and denominator groups must be non-empty and disjoint. A named balance can be referenced in another formula to include all its parts, regardless of their signs. Forward references are allowed, but circular references and ambiguous names shared by balances and parts are rejected.

With `fill = TRUE`, supplied balances are preserved in their original order. If they are compatible with a hierarchical SBP, the hierarchy is completed by adding balances. Compatibility means that each pair involves disjoint sets of parts, or one balance lies wholly within one group of the other. Otherwise, QR decomposition supplies an orthonormal basis for the orthogonal complement of the supplied balances within the clr-plane. These added columns sum to zero and are orthogonal to all supplied columns, but need not be balances.

Completion adds `D - 1 - r` columns, where `D` is the number of parts and `r` is the rank of the supplied balances. The result is orthonormal if the supplied balances are mutually orthogonal. Non-orthogonal inputs are kept and produce a warning unless `silent = TRUE`. Linearly dependent inputs are also kept: completion then returns a redundant generating system rather than a basis, and warns accordingly. Without completion, an incomplete collection also produces a warning unless `silent = TRUE`.

Examples

X <- data.frame(
  a = 1:2, b = 2:3, c = 4:5,
  d = 5:6, e = 10:11, f = 100:101, g = 1:2
)

# Sequential SBP construction
sbp_basis(list(
  b1 = a ~ b + c + d + e + f + g,
  b2 = b ~ c + d + e + f + g,
  b3 = c ~ d + e + f + g,
  b4 = d ~ e + f + g,
  b5 = e ~ f + g,
  b6 = f ~ g
), data = X)
#>           b1         b2         b3         b4         b5         b6
#> a  0.9258201  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> b -0.1543033  0.9128709  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> c -0.1543033 -0.1825742  0.8944272  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> d -0.1543033 -0.1825742 -0.2236068  0.8660254  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> e -0.1543033 -0.1825742 -0.2236068 -0.2886751  0.8164966  0.0000000
#> f -0.1543033 -0.1825742 -0.2236068 -0.2886751 -0.4082483  0.7071068
#> g -0.1543033 -0.1825742 -0.2236068 -0.2886751 -0.4082483 -0.7071068

# Chain construction
sbp_basis(list(
  b1 = a ~ b,
  b2 = b1 ~ c,
  b3 = b2 ~ d,
  b4 = b3 ~ e,
  b5 = b4 ~ f,
  b6 = b5 ~ g
), data = X)
#>           b1         b2         b3         b4         b5         b6
#> a  0.7071068  0.4082483  0.2886751  0.2236068  0.1825742  0.1543033
#> b -0.7071068  0.4082483  0.2886751  0.2236068  0.1825742  0.1543033
#> c  0.0000000 -0.8164966  0.2886751  0.2236068  0.1825742  0.1543033
#> d  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.8660254  0.2236068  0.1825742  0.1543033
#> e  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.8944272  0.1825742  0.1543033
#> f  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.9128709  0.1543033
#> g  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.9258201

# Formula parts can be inferred when data is not supplied
sbp_basis(list(
  b1 = a ~ b,
  b2 = b1 ~ c
))
#>           b1         b2
#> a  0.7071068  0.4082483
#> b -0.7071068  0.4082483
#> c  0.0000000 -0.8164966

# Complete a partial hierarchy with further balances
B_sbp <- sbp_basis(list(ab = a ~ b), data = letters[1:4], fill = TRUE)
B_sbp
#>           ab        .b2        .b3
#> a  0.7071068  0.4082483  0.2886751
#> b -0.7071068  0.4082483  0.2886751
#> c  0.0000000 -0.8164966  0.2886751
#> d  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.8660254
crossprod(B_sbp)
#>                ab          .b2           .b3
#> ab   1.000000e+00 1.844191e-17 -1.695163e-18
#> .b2  1.844191e-17 1.000000e+00  1.076573e-17
#> .b3 -1.695163e-18 1.076573e-17  1.000000e+00

# Orthogonal balances with crossing groups: complete by QR
# The added .q5 column is a general log-contrast, not a balance
B_qr <- sbp_basis(list(
  ef = e ~ f,
  cd = c ~ d,
  aef = a + e + f ~ b + c + d,
  ab = a + b ~ c + d + e + f
), data = letters[1:6], fill = TRUE)
round(B_qr, 3)
#>       ef     cd    aef     ab    .q5
#> a  0.000  0.000  0.408  0.577 -0.577
#> b  0.000  0.000 -0.408  0.577  0.577
#> c  0.000  0.707 -0.408 -0.289 -0.289
#> d  0.000 -0.707 -0.408 -0.289 -0.289
#> e  0.707  0.000  0.408 -0.289  0.289
#> f -0.707  0.000  0.408 -0.289  0.289
crossprod(B_qr)
#>               ef            cd           aef           ab
#> ef  1.000000e+00  0.000000e+00  1.844191e-17 1.695163e-18
#> cd  0.000000e+00  1.000000e+00 -1.844191e-17 1.695163e-18
#> aef 1.844191e-17 -1.844191e-17  1.000000e+00 5.382864e-18
#> ab  1.695163e-18  1.695163e-18  5.382864e-18 1.000000e+00
#> .q5 1.045650e-16  1.695163e-18 -6.458532e-17 1.619798e-16
#>               .q5
#> ef   1.045650e-16
#> cd   1.695163e-18
#> aef -6.458532e-17
#> ab   1.619798e-16
#> .q5  1.000000e+00

# Non-orthogonal inputs are preserved; completion warns
B_nonorthogonal <- sbp_basis(list(ab = a ~ b, bc = b ~ c),
                            data = letters[1:4], fill = TRUE)
#> Warning: Given basis is not orthogonal
crossprod(B_nonorthogonal)
#>                ab            bc          .q3
#> ab   1.000000e+00 -5.000000e-01 1.695163e-18
#> bc  -5.000000e-01  1.000000e+00 1.695163e-18
#> .q3  1.695163e-18  1.695163e-18 1.000000e+00

# Dependent inputs are also preserved, producing a redundant system
B_redundant <- sbp_basis(list(ab = a ~ b, ab_again = a ~ b),
                        data = letters[1:4], fill = TRUE)
#> Warning: Given partition is not a basis
dim(B_redundant)
#> [1] 4 4

# Non-orthogonal system of balances
sbp_basis(list(
  b1 = a + b + c ~ e + f + g,
  b2 = d ~ a + b + c,
  b3 = d ~ e + g,
  b4 = a ~ e + b,
  b5 = b ~ f,
  b6 = c ~ g
), data = X)
#> Warning: Given basis is not orthogonal
#>           b1         b2         b3         b4         b5         b6
#> a  0.4082483 -0.2886751  0.0000000  0.8164966  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> b  0.4082483 -0.2886751  0.0000000 -0.4082483  0.7071068  0.0000000
#> c  0.4082483 -0.2886751  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.7071068
#> d  0.0000000  0.8660254  0.8164966  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> e -0.4082483  0.0000000 -0.4082483 -0.4082483  0.0000000  0.0000000
#> f -0.4082483  0.0000000  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.7071068  0.0000000
#> g -0.4082483  0.0000000 -0.4082483  0.0000000  0.0000000 -0.7071068

# Direct construction from a contrast matrix
sbp_basis(cbind(
  c( 1,  1, -1, -1),
  c( 1, -1,  1, -1),
  c( 1, -1, -1,  1)
))
#>      b1   b2   b3
#> c1  0.5  0.5  0.5
#> c2  0.5 -0.5 -0.5
#> c3 -0.5  0.5 -0.5
#> c4 -0.5 -0.5  0.5
